phrase.payroll_with_pension: For a gross salary of {gross} GEL, the employee takes home {net} GEL. You withhold {pension} GEL for their pension (2%) and {tax} GEL income tax (20% of what's left). On top of the salary you also pay a {employer_pension} GEL employer pension contribution, so this salary costs you {cost} GEL in total.
phrase.payroll_no_pension: For a gross salary of {gross} GEL, the employee takes home {net} GEL after {tax} GEL income tax (20%). No pension contributions apply, since they're not in the funded pension scheme.
phrase.payroll_ask: Sure, I can work that out. What is the gross monthly salary?
phrase.vat_yes: Yes, you need to register for VAT. Your taxable sales over the last 12 months are above GEL 100,000, so you have 2 business days to apply to the tax authority (Revenue Service). VAT applies starting with the sale that took you over the limit.
phrase.vat_no: No, you don't need to register.
phrase.vat_depends: It depends on your turnover. Registration becomes mandatory once taxable sales over any 12 consecutive months exceed GEL 100,000.
phrase.vat_inclusive: {gross} GEL including VAT contains {vat} GEL of VAT, so the price without VAT is {net} GEL. (VAT is 18% of the net price, which is 18/118 of a VAT-inclusive total.)
phrase.vat_exclusive: VAT at 18% on {net} GEL is {vat} GEL, so the total with VAT is {gross} GEL.
phrase.vat_ask_inclusive: Sure. Does {amount} GEL already include VAT, or does VAT come on top?
phrase.distribution: If the company pays out {amount} GEL in dividends, it owes {profit_tax} GEL profit tax: the payout is grossed up (divided by 0.85) and taxed at 15%, so the distribution costs the company {cost} GEL in total.
phrase.dividend_withheld: When paying it, you withhold {withholding} GEL dividend tax (5%), so the owner receives {net} GEL.
phrase.distribution_ask: In Georgia a company pays profit tax only when it distributes profit, not while it keeps it. The payout is divided by 0.85 and taxed at 15%, and 5% is withheld from dividends paid to individuals. How much do you want to pay out?
phrase.small_business_1: On {income} GEL of income you pay {tax} GEL: as a small business, taxable income is taxed at 1%, which leaves you {net} GEL. File the return and pay by the 15th of the following month.
phrase.small_business_3: On {income} GEL of income you pay {tax} GEL, leaving {net} GEL. Since your gross income this year has passed GEL 500,000, the rate is 3% from the month the limit was exceeded until the end of the year. File the return and pay by the 15th of the following month.
phrase.small_business_ask: As a small business you pay 1% of taxable income (3% once the year's gross income passes GEL 500,000). How much did you earn this month?
phrase.vat_payable: You pay {payable} GEL VAT for the month: {output} GEL charged on sales minus {input} GEL deductible VAT on purchases. Only VAT backed by a tax invoice (or an import declaration) can be deducted.
phrase.vat_refund: There's no VAT to pay this month: the deductible VAT on purchases ({input} GEL) is more than the VAT on sales ({output} GEL). The {refund} GEL difference can be refunded (Art. 181).
phrase.vat_payable_ask_output: Sure. VAT payable is the VAT you charged on sales minus the deductible VAT on purchases. How much VAT did you charge on your sales this month?
phrase.vat_payable_ask_input: Got it: {output} GEL VAT on sales. And how much deductible VAT is on your purchases this month (from tax invoices)?
phrase.need: To answer that I need a bit more information:
phrase.no_rules: I don't have a rule in effect for that on the selected date.
assumption.pension_participant: I've assumed the employee is in the funded pension scheme, as most employees are. Tell me if they're not.
assumption.dividend_recipient: I've assumed the dividend goes to an individual owner. Dividends paid to another company aren't taxed at source, so tell me if that's the case.
assumption.over_small_business_limit: I've assumed your gross income this year is still within GEL 500,000. If it's higher, tell me: the rate is then 3%.
assumption.books.taxable_turnover_12m: I used the sales recorded in your books: {amount} GEL (without VAT) over the last 12 months. If some sales aren't recorded, tell me the real total.
assumption.books.over_small_business_lim: Your books show {amount} GEL of income this year so far, and I compared that with the GEL 500,000 limit.

phrase.penalty_interest: Penalty interest is {interest} GEL: 0.05% of {tax} GEL for each overdue day ({late}), so {total} GEL in all.
phrase.penalty_fine: If the return is filed that late too, add a fine of {fine} GEL: 5% of the tax for each started month, 10% once it's more than 2 months.
phrase.penalty_fine_only: The fine for filing the return late is {fine} GEL: 5% of {tax} GEL for each started month, 10% once it's more than 2 months. If the tax was paid late as well, tell me how many days late and I'll add the penalty interest.
